reviewer_notes: Independent re-derivation. Anchors used: raw-byte PE parse (own Python parser), llvm-readobj/llvm-objdump on patched COPIES, impcallers/xref/strx/guid on RoGetActivationFactory/WaitForSingleObjectEx/0x13f794.. globals/IID bytes, game-side vtable walk from SoundSystemFMOD (0x136AF94) and SoundEngine::ctor (0x53CDA4), simulation of ntdll ARM_MOV32T base relocation on the patched images. Work files: arm32/work/fmod_verify/ (fmod_ARM_finder.dll = finder's 3 edits, fmod_ARM_alt.dll = reloc-safe variant, mkpatch.py, pe_imports_dump.py, orig/patched import dumps). Win10-ARM32 desktop behaviour was checked only through a Win11 x64 names-only proxy (apiset + export tables); Windows RT 8.1 and every runtime/audible claim are not verifiable on this machine.

verdicts.note: sha256sum fmod_ARM.dll = 5f92f5ac9317c7a5d61ab6b43a2e799ae90eb7eee5c992c85d0325ba1d09fc38, size 1118720, machine 0x1C4, ImageBase 0x10000000, SizeOfImage 0x153000 (1388544), EP 0xAEE49, DllCharacteristics 0x1140, CheckSum 0, no cert dir. Version literal 0x00010904 sits at DLL RVA 0x945C0 (pc-relative load in sub_945A8 = System::getVersion body) and the game's createSystem (0x5A393C) compares against the same 0x10904 (pool 0x5A3988): exactly the minimum, as claimed.

Own parser: 27 descriptors, 129 imported symbols (llvm-readobj --coff-imports also 129), directory RVA 0xFA330 -> file 0xF8D30, 20-byte descriptors. Every DLL-name string file offset in the finder's table reproduced from raw bytes (e.g. winrt 0xF929C, winrt-string 0xF92BE, MMDevAPI 0xF92E6, MFPlat 0xF93A2, MFReadWrite 0xF93D4, VCRUNTIME140_APP 0xF989A, crt-* 0xF9AC8.., sysinfo 0xF9C92, interlocked 0xF9CB6). Desktop check (Win11 x64 proxy, GetProcAddress of every named import on the apiset/real DLL): ALL 26 other DLLs resolve with all names; LoadLibrary('VCRUNTIME140_APP.dll') fails with error 126 and no such file exists in System32; MMDevAPI export ordinal 17 = ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync (llvm-readobj --coff-exports of System32\MMDevAPI.dll). Only WinRT-ish imports: winrt-l1-1-0 {RoGetActivationFactory cell 0xB118C, RoUninitialize 0xB1190, RoInitialize 0xB1194}, winrt-string {CompareStringOrdinal 0xB119C, CreateStringReference 0xB11A0, GetStringRawBuffer 0xB11A4}; LoadPackagedLibrary is called only from sub_79A20 (impcallers) and the game does not import FMOD LoadPlugin.

Windows RT 8.1 (processthreads-l1-1-2, file-l1-2-1, file-l2-1-1, libraryloader-l2-1-0, sysinfo-l1-2-1, UCRT presence) cannot be checked here. The in-place contingency (rename those api-set names to KERNEL32.dll) is sound as far as I can test: all 11 functions of those contracts are exported by this machine's kernel32 (CreateThread, SetThreadPriority, GetCurrentThreadId, GetCurrentProcessId, IsProcessorFeaturePresent, ReadFile, CreateFile2, SetFilePointerEx, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, LoadPackagedLibrary, GetSystemTimeAsFileTime). Same caveat applies to the exe itself (UCRT/MSVCP140_APP).

Raw bytes at file 0xF989A = 'VCRUNTIME140_APP.dll\0' (21 bytes) followed by a pad 00 and the next hint/name entry (00 19 'qsort'); writing 'VCRUNTIME140.dll\0' + 4 NULs only touches the 21 bytes. Patched copy parses with llvm-readobj: descriptor #17 name = VCRUNTIME140.dll, still 11 symbols, all 129 imports intact; the only diff of --coff-imports vs. the original is that name. The 11 names (memcmp, __CxxFrameHandler3, memcpy, _purecall, __C_specific_handler, __std_type_info_destroy_list, __std_exception_copy/destroy, memset, _CxxThrowException, memmove) all resolve in System32 vcruntime140.dll (x64 proxy).

DllCharacteristics u16 at file 0x17E (= e_lfanew 0x120 + 24 + 70) reads 40 11; after 40 01 llvm-readobj shows 0x140 (DYNAMIC_BASE|NX_COMPAT), APPCONTAINER cleared. NEW: this edit is optional hardening - I loaded a copy of System32\version.dll with APPCONTAINER (0x1000) set into a desktop python process on Win11 x64 and LoadLibrary succeeded, so the loader does not reject AppContainer-flagged DLLs in a normal process (ARM32 loader not testable, same code family). Keeping the edit is harmless.

Descriptor #1 name string at file 0xF929C ('api-ms-win-core-winrt-l1-1-0.dll', 32 chars + NUL), IAT RVA 0xB118C; 'win32craft.dll' (15 B) fits. Agree that option B is dominated by the IAT hook (B') because win32craft.dll's current RoGetActivationFactory (api_compat.c:429) is a REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG stub and RoInitialize/RoUninitialize are only combase forwarders.

Cell RVAs reproduced from the import tables and from the disassembly of sub_79300 (movw/movt 0x100B118C = RoGetActivationFactory, 0x100B1160 = WaitForSingleObjectEx, 0x100B115C = CreateEventExW). IAT lives in .rdata (0xB1000) so a host hook must VirtualProtect the cell (arm32_patch_cell does).

Export System::init (0x6D8D9, thumb of sub_6D8D8) -> sub_971C0 (handle lookup) -> sub_945C4 (call at 0x94608 to sub_89024) -> sub_89024 (refcounted OS init: 3x sub_78FA0 = InitializeCriticalSectionEx, then bl sub_79300 at 0x8905C; nonzero result returns without bumping the counter). The only 0x1C (FMOD_ERR_INTERNAL) producers in sub_79300 are the WinRT HRESULT<0 and CreateEventExW==NULL branches. FMOD_System_Create (0x7E905) path never calls sub_79300.

Re-decoded sub_79300 (0x79300..0x799C8) independently. MediaDevice (len 0x21): RoGetActivationFactory IID 0xDD7BC, vtable slot 13 (+0x34) add_DefaultAudioRenderDeviceChanged(handler, &token) with token = 0x13F794+0x24. DeviceInformation (len 0x2D) IID 0xDD870, slot 13 (+0x34) CreateWatcher(DeviceClass 2 then 1); watcher slots 6/8/10/12 (+0x18/+0x20/+0x28/+0x30) add_Added/Updated/Removed/EnumerationCompleted, slot 17 (+0x44) Start, then WaitForSingleObjectEx(event [r7+0x4c], r2=0, r1=mvns r2 = 0xFFFFFFFF) at 0x795F6 and 0x79634; EnumerationCompleted handler built by sub_7881C from the event handle and its Invoke (sub_7A018) is SetEvent([this+0xC]); watchers stored to 0x13F794+0x18/+0x1C. Package: sub_78618/sub_786D0, factory slot 6 (+0x18) get_Current, IPackage slot 7 (+0x1C) InstalledLocation, QI IStorageItem {4207A996-..} (0xDD6F4), slot 12 (+0x30) get_Path -> sub_73210 (wcsdup) -> [0x13F794+0]. ApplicationData: IApplicationData slot 14 (+0x38) TemporaryFolder -> +4, slot 12 (+0x30) LocalFolder -> +8, slot 13 (+0x34) RoamingFolder -> +0xC. SDK vtable orders agree. Failure cmp/blt branches all end in movs r4,#0x1C. See headline.hang_risk for a correction about how special the INFINITE wait is.

Decoded the raw GUID bytes: 0xDD6F4 IStorageItem {4207A996-CA2F-42F7-BDE8-8B10457A7F30}, 0xDD704 IPackageStatics {4E534BDF-2960-4878-97A4-9624DEB72F2D}, 0xDD7BC IMediaDeviceStatics {AA2D9A40-909F-4BBA-BF8B-0C0D296F14F0}, 0xDD870 IDeviceInformationStatics {C17F100E-3A46-4A78-8013-769DC9B97390}, 0xDD860 IApplicationDataStatics {5612147B-E843-45E3-94D8-06169E3C8E17}, 0xDE4B4 IMarshal, 0xDE2AC IAgileObject. The DLL contains exactly four 'Windows.*' class strings (Package, ApplicationData, MediaDevice, DeviceInformation); Package and ApplicationData each have refs=1 (sub_79300 only), i.e. the only package-identity-dependent activations are the two that the 6-byte/4-byte patch skips.

xref scan of 0x13F790..0x13F7C8: the base 0x13F794 is referenced only by sub_790BC (4x, offsets +0,+4,+8,+0xC), sub_79300 and sub_79AF0; 0x13F7A4/0x13F7A8 are separate flag words (sub_78F60/79FEC/7A034/7BAA0/7C510, device-changed flags set by the handlers), 0x13F7C0 is another object. sub_790BC (FMOD_OS_File_Open prefix expansion for ms-appx://, ms-appdata:///temp|local|roaming) is reached only via sub_709FC; with NULL globals it would call sub_73290(dst, NULL, 0xFF) = immediate NULL read, so the finder's caveat is right. The game never reaches it: setFileSystem installs 4 user callbacks (sub_5A2A7C/5A2B84/5A2BA8/5A2C24) and the only 'ms-appx:///data/' string in the exe is used by AppPlatform_Winrt::vf4 (0x582856), not passed to FMOD.

sub_79AF0 (shutdown) null-checks +0x1C/+0x18 watchers, the token pair at +0x24/+0x28 (re-activates MediaDevice with the REAL factory to unregister only if nonzero) and each of the four path pointers before the free helper, so NULL path globals are safe. RoInitialize(1 = RO_INIT_MULTITHREADED)/RoUninitialize appear only in the FMOD thread trampoline sub_79D24 (0x79D4E/0x79D60).

Static part reproduced: sub_7B364 activates MediaDevice and DeviceInformation again (real factories), creates an event, builds the list with its own async wait (sub_7A598 -> WaitForSingleObjectEx INFINITE) and uses WindowsCompareStringOrdinal; sub_7BAA0 calls MFStartup (0x7BB52) and MFLockSharedWorkQueue (0x7BB78) and reaches ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync through the ordinal-17 thunk (sub_7BC84, callers 0x7BC98/0x7BCA6, also sub_7C9E0); IAudioClient2 IID {726778CD-..} is present at 0xDF418 (5 refs). Runtime behaviour (audible output, device activation on desktop/RT) is NOT verifiable here.

Functionally reproduced: bytes at 0x78A50 are bb65 4df21871; 00 24 00 F0 85 B9 decodes (capstone + llvm-objdump) as movs r4,#0 / b.w 0x79960; 0x79960 is the common cleanup tail (releases +0x68/+0x6C/+0x70 delegate regs, event wrapper, +0x34/+0x30/+0x38/+0x3C) and returns r4 = 0 exactly like the normal success path (0x798C6 movs r4,#0; b 0x79918); the skipped cleanup slots (+0x40/+0x50/+0x54/+0x58) are not yet initialised at that point, so skipping is correct. Patched copy parses as a valid PE (llvm-readobj: 129 imports, 1087 exports, 6796 base relocs unchanged, DllCharacteristics 0x140). CORRECTION (missed by finder): the 6 bytes straddle a base relocation. .reloc has an IMAGE_REL_BASED_ARM_MOV32T (type 7) entry at RVA 0x79652 (the original movw/movt r1 pair) so the loader will rewrite 8 bytes starting at the b.w. I simulated the ntdll fix-up for deltas 0, 0x23450000, 0xFFFF0000: the b.w survives unchanged only because every load delta is a multiple of 64 KiB (movw half unchanged) - it is correct today but fragile reasoning. Reloc-safe alternative that touches no relocated bytes: file 0x78A4E, 4 bytes 00 23 BB 65 (movs r3,#0; str r3,[r7,#0x58]) -> 00 24 86 E1 (movs r4,#0; b.n 0x79960, imm11 0x186), RVA 0x7964E; no branch targets 0x7964E..0x79657 (scanned); verified by capstone/llvm-objdump and by the relocation simulation (sha256 of that image with edits 1+2: cf226ecb83f478a67c6dab205dbd2a5ed0a469ac9fa27f2ed4bda12680d5d1f6; finder's variant: c0e9caee152f9f9819a4f43691c800effad03ae958f40d558fec90c9e5d5ec47).

Design is sound and the site is right: sub_79300 loads the cell 0xB118C at 0x7935A and 0x79400 and calls it as RoGetActivationFactory(HSTRING r0, REFIID r1, void** r2); win32_get_activation_factory (win32_host.c:7517) takes an LPCWSTR (not an HSTRING) so the hook must first get the raw buffer via native WindowsGetStringRawBuffer, as the finder says. Fakes match FMOD's slots: package_vtable has slot 7, appdata_vtable slots 12/13/14 (all fake_appdata_local_folder), folder vtables slot 12 fake_folder_path, fake_query_interface default returns self (so QI IStorageItem works). The HSTRING returned by fake_folder_path is created by api_compat WindowsCreateString, whose native forward is gated on SizeOfImage == 0x02DB1000 (api_compat.c:150-165) - on ARM (0x01731000) it would return a fake-format HSTRING that FMOD's native WindowsGetStringRawBuffer cannot read; PORT_RULES #8 requirement is real. Not run on a device.

All 39 names in null_impl_table equal the exe's fmod_ARM.dll import names (set diff empty) and all 39 are exported by the real DLL. I re-derived the ABI at the call sites for: getVersion/createSystem (bool, <0x10904 fails), init(0x20,4,NULL), set3DSettings (s0,s1,s2), createChannelGroup x2 (+0x7C/+0x80), getMasterChannelGroup (+0x78), addGroup (this=[+0x78], r1=[+0x7C]/[+0x80], r2=1, r3=NULL), setFileSystem (open r1, close r2, read r3, seek [sp], asyncread [sp+4]=NULL, asynccancel [sp+8]=NULL, blockalign [sp+12]=-1), createStream/createSound (r1 name, r2 mode, r3 exinfo=NULL, [sp]=Sound**), getNumDrivers/getDriverInfo/setDriver/setOutput (only when the preferred-device GUID first dword != 0, selectDriver 0x5A3890; getDriverInfo has 4 stack args), getFormat (soundFormatAccepted 0x5A3210: (&type,NULL,NULL,NULL), rejects 9 and 0x12), getSoftwareFormat(&rate,NULL,NULL), getDSPClock(NULL,&local), addFadePoint(r2:r3,s0), setDelay(start r2:r3, end [sp],[sp+4], bool [sp+8]), isPlaying (byte pre-zeroed by the caller). I did not trace every one of the remaining ~20 trivial setters (setMute/setPaused/setPitch/setVolume/set3DAttributes/stop/...), whose signatures follow directly from the MSVC-ARM mangled names. Object-lifetime notes (static handles, sound cache keyed by name, loadSound only caches when type accepted) are consistent with loadSound (0x5A3BD0) and sub_5A4F48.

xref of vtable 0x136AF94 = single hit in sub_5A33C8 (SoundSystemFMOD ctor, base vtable 0x1367880 first), which SoundEngine::ctor (0x53CDA4) calls on this+8 (0x53CE30). RTTI has only SoundSystemBase and SoundSystemFMOD; there is no other SoundSystem implementation and no selector.

SoundEngine::ctor tail (0x53CF14..0x53D012): vtbl+4 createSystem (0x5A393C: FMOD_System_Create(&this+0x74) via stub 0x5A3880, getVersion >= 0x10904, return bool); if true: vtbl+0x10 selectDriver(preferred GUID), vtbl+8 init (0x5A398C: System::init(0x20,4,NULL); on error call no-op logger sub_5A31BC and return; success tail: setFileSystem, set3DSettings, createChannelGroup 'Sound Channel Group' -> +0x7C and 'Music Channel Group' -> +0x80, getMasterChannelGroup -> +0x78, addGroup x2, strb 1 -> +0x70), then vtbl+0x34/+0x30 volume setters. init's return value is ignored by the ctor.

Graceful, never crash/assert. sub_5A31BC only formats ('%s(%d): FMOD error %d - %s') and discards. Guards on +0x74 (System*) and +0x70 (flag) verified at the head of loadSound (0x5A3BF4/0x5A3C06 -> exit path 0x5A41E4), playByName, update (vf30), vf12/13/15/19/21/22/24/31, shutdown. Channel-handle users (vf18/26/27/28/33/35/37) have no explicit guard but operate on handles that only exist after a successful loadSound/play. Note: with edit set D init succeeds, so this path only matters for options A/C failures.

ARM game: AudioGraphSettings is created in audiograph:createSettings (0x5992B8, category 9 = AudioRenderCategory::Speech) from audiograph:init_tts_graph (0x59871C), called from AppPlatform_Winrt::ctor (0x581EF6) next to the SpeechSynthesizer strings; the continuation (0x5988CC) is the TTS pipeline. FMOD is unconditional. Hence the x86 host comment (win32_host.c:6872 'falls back to its FMOD path') describes a Windows-7 fake for the TTS graph, not an audio-backend selector, and no ARM fake is needed for FMOD. Cross-unit note: on Win10 ARM32 the real AudioGraph activation should work, so whether to fake it is a platform_fixes/iat_hooks decision unrelated to audio output.

ARM exe delay-import directory (0x131F20C) lists only api-ms-win-gaming-tcui-l1-1-0/1-2.dll; fmod_ARM.dll is normal import descriptor #1 (descriptor file 0x1325DBC, Name field 0x1325DC8 = 0x013283EA -> string at file 0x13277EA, 'fmod_ARM.dll' + one pad byte before the next hint entry => max 13 chars in place). The x86 load_real_fmod/bridge_fmod_* layer (win32_host.c ~1487-1950) has no ARM counterpart.

FMOD imports exactly three HSTRING functions (WindowsCompareStringOrdinal, WindowsCreateStringReference, WindowsGetStringRawBuffer) from api-ms-win-core-winrt-string-l1-1-0 = real combase, and never WindowsDeleteString. For B' every HSTRING FMOD receives from host fakes must be a native HSTRING (WindowsCreateString forward to combase); api_compat.c native_hstring_proc gate needs the ARM image-size constant.

Imprecise headline. What is true: the only package-identity-dependent activations (Package, ApplicationData) exist once, in sub_79300. But real WinRT (MediaDevice, DeviceInformation, ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync, MF work queues) is used in four more places: output start-up (sub_7B364/sub_7A384/sub_7BAA0, i.e. inside System::init after sub_79300), System::update -> sub_7C510 -> sub_7BE70 whenever a device-changed flag (0x13F7A8) is set, getNumDrivers/getDriverInfo list building (not reached by default), and shutdown sub_79AF0. RoGetActivationFactory import callers: sub_78690, sub_786D0, sub_79300 (x2), sub_79AF0, sub_7A384, sub_7B364, sub_7BE70 (x2).

The INFINITE wait (r2=0; mvns r1,r2) is real at 0x795F6/0x79634, but it is not a special new risk of sub_79300: the identical idiom WaitForSingleObjectEx(h, INFINITE) occurs at 0x7A5E0 (device list), 0x79D0E (thread join), 0x7B99E, 0x7BC16 (ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync completion), 0x7C462, 0x7C74A (and a counted wait at 0x7C97A). Patching/avoiding the two waits in sub_79300 therefore would not remove the hang exposure of options A/D/B'; only option C (no real FMOD) does. Mitigating facts the finder did not list: host calls RoInitialize(RO_INIT_MULTITHREADED) in Win32Bootstrap (win32_host.c:14910) before the game builds the SoundEngine, and FMOD's delegates aggregate the free-threaded marshaler (CoCreateFreeThreadedMarshaler in sub_78AA0, IMarshal IID 0xDE4B4, IAgileObject 0xDE2AC), so the usual 'callback needs the blocked STA' deadlock does not apply. A timeout is also non-fatal if ever wanted: WaitForSingleObjectEx returns 0x102 (>0) and the code only fails on result < 0.

Keep D as primary (cheapest; I could not find a cheaper or more robust real-audio option) but ship it with the reloc-safe code patch (file 0x78A4E, 00 23 BB 65 -> 00 24 86 E1) instead of 0x78A50 (finder's bytes work only through the 64 KiB-delta argument), and treat edit (2) APPCONTAINER-clear as optional. Rejected cheaper variants: (a) return 0 at sub_79300 entry (4 bytes at 0x79300: 00 20 70 47) also avoids the first two device-watcher waits and the real MediaDevice/DeviceInformation handlers but loses hot-plug/default-device-change handling (flags 0x13F7A4/0x13F7A8 stay 0) and does not remove the other INFINITE waits, so it buys little; (b) capping INFINITE needs >2 bytes per site (movs r1,#imm8 only gives <=255 ms) so it would require an IAT-wrapper in the host - not worth it. Add one cheap robustness feature: a host/package switch that selects the silent stub (see option C0) so a hang on a particular device is recoverable without a rebuild.

The finder's wiring (ii) (repoint exe descriptor #1 Name RVA to a string in a new section) is workable but unnecessary and needs a new exe section. Cheaper form 'C0': build a tiny standalone ARM32 stub DLL named fmod_ARM.dll (39 exports via a .def 'mangled=c_name' list, no imports at all, therefore no VCRUNTIME/UCRT/WinRT dependency, no exe edit, no win32craft.dll change) and ship it instead of the real fmod_ARM.dll; the same stub can optionally LoadLibrary a renamed patched real DLL and forward (x86-style bridge, win32_host.c load_real_fmod/bridge_fmod_*) with fallback to silence if System_Create/init fails. Effort ~2 h for the stub, ~6-8 h for the hybrid.

missing: Base-relocation overlap of the 6-byte code patch: .reloc type-7 (ARM_MOV32T) entry at RVA 0x79652 sits inside the patched bytes; safe only because load deltas are 64 KiB multiples. A 4-byte patch at 0x7964E (00 24 86 E1) avoids it entirely (see fmod.patch_skip_package_appdata).

The INFINITE-wait idiom is present at >= 6 other sites (0x7A5E0, 0x79D0E, 0x7B99E, 0x7BC16, 0x7C462, 0x7C74A) so hang risk is intrinsic to every real-FMOD option; mitigated by MTA RoInitialize in Win32Bootstrap and agile (FTM+IAgileObject) delegates.

System::init continues with output start-up (sub_7B364/sub_7BAA0) after sub_79300; D does not guarantee init success, only that package identity is no longer needed. If output start-up fails FMOD returns an error and the game goes silent gracefully (confirmed), so D degrades to A's behaviour, not to a crash.

Hot-plug/default-device-change handling relies on the handlers installed in sub_79300 steps 1-2 (flags 0x13F7A4/0x13F7A8 consumed by sub_78F60/sub_7C510 -> sub_7BE70 which re-activates real MediaDevice/DeviceInformation inside System::update); unaffected by patch D, lost by the 'return at entry' variant.
The exe's FMOD import cannot be redirected to a longer DLL name in place (13-char limit incl. pad); the stub-named-fmod_ARM.dll route needs no exe edit at all.
APPCONTAINER flag is not a load blocker for DLLs on a desktop process (tested on Win11 x64): edit (2) is optional.
api_compat.c native_hstring_proc gate (SizeOfImage == 0x02DB1000) is a prerequisite not only for B/B' but for any host code that hands HSTRINGs to native FMOD; for option D/C it is not needed.

Could not verify on this machine: Windows RT 8.1 api-set availability, whether DeviceWatcher EnumerationCompleted fires in an unpackaged ARM32 desktop process, whether ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync works from the game's thread, and audible output. An on-device run of the patched DLL with win32craft.log (host should log GetModuleHandleW(L"fmod_ARM.dll") before SoundEngine creation) is the decisive test.
recommendation_check: Primary D is the right call (cheapest, no host code, real audio, game degrades silently on any init failure), with two changes: use the reloc-safe 4-byte code patch at file 0x78A4E (00 23 BB 65 -> 00 24 86 E1) instead of the 6-byte one, and regard the APPCONTAINER edit as optional. B' remains the right fallback if real package paths are ever needed (needs combase HSTRING forwarding because fake_folder_path returns host-created HSTRINGs). The finder's claim that C is the only option without hang risk is correct, but the finder under-stated how general the INFINITE-wait exposure is (7 sites, not 2) and over-stated its novelty; the real mitigations are the MTA RoInitialize already done by the host plus a way to fall back to silence. Cheapest robust fallback is C0 (stand-alone stub shipped as fmod_ARM.dll, no exe or win32craft.dll change); a hybrid stub that forwards to the patched real DLL and falls back to silence on System_Create/init failure is the most robust but costs ~3x more. Final edit set for D (original sha256 5f92f5ac9317c7a5d61ab6b43a2e799ae90eb7eee5c992c85d0325ba1d09fc38): (1) file 0xF989A 21 B 'VCRUNTIME140_APP.dll\0' -> 'VCRUNTIME140.dll\0' + 4 NUL; (2, optional) file 0x17E 40 11 -> 40 01; (3) file 0x78A4E 00 23 BB 65 -> 00 24 86 E1 (resulting file sha256 with all three: cf226ecb83f478a67c6dab205dbd2a5ed0a469ac9fa27f2ed4bda12680d5d1f6, kept in arm32/work/fmod_verify/fmod_ARM_alt.dll; finder variant c0e9caee152f9f9819a4f43691c800effad03ae958f40d558fec90c9e5d5ec47).
